full_judgment:
37. We shall now deal with the contention of the contemnor No. 1 that the freedom of the press as guaranteed under Article 39 of the Constitution ousts the jurisdiction of this Court to assume contempt proceedings. The freedom of press as guaranteed under Article 39(2) is subject to reasonable restriction imposed by law in relation to contempt of Court. Article 7(2) of the Constitution provides that the Constitution is the supreme law of the land. Article 108 of the Constitution empowers the Apex Court with the authority to order for the investigation of or punishment for any contempt of this Court. Therefore, having read Article 39(2) and Article 108 of the Constitution together, we are of the view that freedom of press guaranteed under Article 39(2) is subject to Article 108 of the Constitution. Article 108 of the Constitution; in no way, is subject to Article 39(2). So, the contention of the contemnor No. 1 that authority of this Court to investigate and punish a contemnor is limited is nothing but fallacious and unjustified argument. The law gives no one a licence to misrepresent the proceedings and orders of the Court, not to speak of allowing to deliberately paint an absolutely wrong and incomplete picture, which has the tendency to scandalise and redicule the Court and bring it into disrepute. The right of criticising, in good faith whether in private or public, an order or judgment of the Court, cannot be excercised with malice or by attempting to impute the administration of justice to disrepute. Freedom of press is the life blood of democracy, but this freedom of press is subject to certain qualification. An offence of scandalising the Court per se is one of such limitations. 

 "Any expression of opinion would not be immune from liability for exceeding the limits under the law of contempt of Court or the constitutional limitations either under the law of defamation or Contempt of Court or the other constitutional limitations under Article 39(2). If a citizen, therefore, in the garb of exercising right of free expression under Article 39(2)(a) and (b), tries to scandalise the Court or undermines the dignity of the Court or makes abusive words, then the Court is under duty to exercise its jurisdiction under Article 108. No person has any right to flout the mandate of law or the authority of the Court for alleged establishment of law under the cloak of freedom of thought and conscience or freedom of speech and expression or the freedom of the press guaranteed by Article 39. Such freedom is subject to reasonable restriction imposed by the law." 

 41. We shall now address the contention of the contemnor No. 1 that there being currently no law relating to contempt of Court, this Court has no authority to punish the contemnor No. 1 for contempt of Court. The entire contention of contemnor No. 1 in this regard is fallacious. The Supreme Court, under Article 108 of the Constitution, is a Court of Record and exercises all powers of such Court including the power to punish for contempt of itself. Supreme Court has power to determine its own jurisdiction and punish for contempt. The provisions of law relating to contempt can only be in addition to and not in derogation to the constitutional provisions under Article 108 of the Constitution and an Act of Parliament cannot limit or regulate the exercise of jurisdiction conferred by the Constitution. The Supreme Court's powers of investigation and punishment under the Constitution as a Court of Record cannot be subjected to other laws. No law can diminish or limit such power. However, in our view, only limitation upon the authority of this Court under Article 108 of the Constitution is that this Court must not infringe any other provisions of the Constitution, neither shall this Court usurp the functions of legislating laws while exercising the authority under Article 108 of the Constitution as a Court of Record, such as creating new offence, imposing punishment upon the contemnor which is not commensurate with the law declared or followed by the Supreme Court. Apart from this limitation this Court, as a Court of Record, has obligation to ensure that decisions/ orders of this Court are kept in permanent form and those are respected by everyone, which inherently couple with the power of this Court to punish those who dare to disrespect the orders/decisions of this Court, and not the least to punish those who dare to disrespect the Court itself. The Supreme Court has an inherent jurisdiction to punish for contempt of Court, We, therefore, hold that this Court being the Court of Record has inherent jurisdiction to punish the contemnor No. 1 for contempt of Court.
